O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Baibhaw Gahlaut, Advocate Order No. 09 Dated: 10.09.2024 The petitioner
apprehending his arrest for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/365 of the Indian Penal
Code and under Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, has prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the complaint.
The petitioner is the son-in-law (Damad) of the opposite party no. 2.

Initially, an F.I.R. being Harla P.S. Case No. 65 of 2015 was lodged by the informant against the petitioner and his family members for the offences punishable under Sections 364/498-A/34 of I.P.C. in which in addition to the demand of dowry and torturing the daughter of the informant, it was also alleged that on 30.03.2015, the petitioner sent a message on the mobile phone of the informant's daughter- Neha Kumari (wife of the petitioner) to meet him.
Accordingly, she met the petitioner at 11:45 a.m. at the place she was called.
The informant and other family members were also there.
However, the petitioner took away the informant' daughter by a motorcycle.
Even after two hours, when the informant's daughter did not return, the informant called her on mobile phone, however the same was found switched-off.

Thereafter, the informant called the petitioner on his mobile no. 8092937239 and asked her whereabouts on which the petitioner flatly said that she did not come with him.
3.

It is further submitted that the said case was investigated by the police and final report was submitted in favour of the petitioner and other accused persons before the concerned court on 11.10.2022 stating that the said case was being closed due to insufficient evidence.

Thereafter, the informant filed protest petition and on finding prima facie case against the petitioner, the court of learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class, Bokaro, vide order dated 14.08.2023, took cognizance for the Vijay Kumar Sah vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45629677/

sentences.text: 4. It is also submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the allegation made by the informant was not found true during the investigation.
Despite the said fact, the order of cognizance dated 14.08.2023 has been passed by learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class, Bokaro.
Hence, the petitioner may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

5. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 opposes the petitioner's prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submits that despite specific allegation made by the informant, the police did not properly investigate the case and informant's daughter has not yet been traced.

6. Learned A.P.P. relying on the case diary submits that sufficient evidence was not found during the investigation against the accused persons as a result of which final report was submitted in their favour.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail.
8.

Accordingly, the petitioner, above named, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the court below within three weeks from today, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class, Bokaro in connection with C.P. Case No. 295 of 2023, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
Ritesh/ (Rajesh Shankar, J.)
